Chapter Details: Status of digitalisation of records in rural facilities
Definition: The status of digital data capture in rural police stations
Comments: No specific evidence found on rural police stations' recording methods. Recent urban innovations like unmanned smart police stations (2026) and Digital Ethiopia 2030 focus on Addis Ababa pilots with digital kiosks for reporting, eliminating paperwork there. Courts have e-filing (2025). However, UNODC reports emphasize training and capacity building without digital case systems; HR reports detail poor conditions in police stations but no digital mentions. Rural areas likely retain traditional paper-based practices (occurrence books, manual files) as digitisation is urban/pilot-focused. Score 1 as broad evidence indicates paper dominance outside pilots.

Definition: The status of digital data capture in rural civil registry offices
Comments: Rural registry offices (kebeles, 92% of operational sites) in Ethiopia rely entirely on paper-based manual registration using bound booklets with carbon copies; original stays local, copies transmitted upward.UNECA CRVS Ethiopia Snapshot Digitalisation limited to urban pilots (100 kebeles in Addis Ababa computerized; tablet ME-CRVS in 1,300 kebeles, fragmented home-grown/open-source systems in regions like Oromia/Amhara).Strengthening CRVS Presentation No evidence of routine point-of-service digital use in most rural facilities; paper default despite national plans for standardization.UNECA Digitalisation Assessment Key barriers: inadequate ICT infrastructure, electricity/network interruptions, rugged terrain limiting access (up to 8hr walks), transport/support lacks, low awareness/demand. National policy (Digital Ethiopia 2030, CRVS Strategy 2022-26, 2025 Proclamation) aims full digital linkage to NID/Fayda ID, but rural reality lags far behind urban pilots due to infrastructure gaps, conflicts reducing kebele ops from 90% to 70%.

Chapter Details: Status of digitalisation of records in rural facilities
Definition: The status of digital data capture in rural primary schools
Comments: Rural primary schools in Ethiopia predominantly use paper-based methods for recording administrative data, attendance, and learning outcomes. Schools complete lengthy annual EMIS census questionnaires (25 pages) by hand, using paper registers that are often poorly maintained or stored insecurely. Data is physically transported to woreda/REB levels for manual Excel entry; no digital tools at point-of-service. Attendance tracked in registers (not centrally digitized), learning outcomes via national exams aggregated later.UNESCO ECW EMIS Case Study%20and%20Data%20for%20Increased%20Resilience%20to%20Crisis_%20country%20case%20study_%20Ethopia.pdf) Only 76-83% of schools use EMIS (declining), with most rural lacking computers (40% have working ones, 28% internet); principals handle manually.RISE GEQIP Report In Oromia (rural-heavy sample), EMIS manual/paper, rated moderate but emerging on infrastructure; shortages in ICT, budget, staff.Oromia EMIS Thesis Digital pilots (SMIS, tablets) exist but isolated/not scaled to majority rural facilities. Barriers: no electricity/computers/internet in most rural schools, low skills, transport issues, no data culture. National EMIS policy ambitious, but rural reality remains paper (score 1); aggregation digitalizes upward reports only.UNESCO ECW EMIS Case Study%20and%20Data%20for%20Increased%20Resilience%20to%20Crisis_%20country%20case%20study_%20Ethopia.pdf)

Chapter Details: Status of digitalisation of records in rural facilities
Definition: The status of digital data capture in rural primary healthcare clinics
Comments: Rural primary healthcare in Ethiopia operates through ~17,900 health posts staffed by Health Extension Workers (HEWs). The electronic Community Health Information System (eCHIS), introduced in 2018, has been scaled to approximately 8,011 health posts (~45% of total) as of 2024, with over 25 million individuals and 6 million households registered. eCHIS is a tablet-based platform covering modules for family folders, RMNCHN, disease prevention, and NCD management. However, actual utilisation remains low: only ~50% of HEWs at equipped posts actively use it, and just 24.5% offer ANC services through the platform. A 2023 maturity assessment rated ICT infrastructure at 1.67/5, citing inadequate power supply, limited connectivity, and insufficient hardware at health posts. DHIS2 covers all 30,000+ public health facilities for aggregate reporting (95%+ completeness), but data at health posts is still primarily collected on paper then entered at district level. EMR systems exist at only 58 public facilities nationally. Key barriers include unreliable electricity and internet at rural health posts, low digital literacy, heavy workloads creating dual paper-digital reporting burdens, and staff turnover. The scale of eCHIS deployment (~45% of health posts) represents meaningful digital presence at point of service, moving beyond entirely paper-based, though paper remains the predominant method.
